newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Road transport body asks France to stop blockages.
newsitem.headline: Road transport body asks France to stop blockages.

text.p: The International Road Transport Union (IRU) said on Tuesday it had called on the French government to put an end to the blockage by striking lorry drivers of foreign traffic passing through the country.
The Geneva-based IRU said it had also appealed to French Transport Minister Bernard Pons to ensure that foreign drivers stranded by the blockades for more than a week were given help.

The body, which links 95 road transport associations in 50 countries, reported it had asked the Swiss and Austrian authorities to suspend restrictions on truck size to allow traffic stranded in southern Europe to move north.

The IRU said it had originally asked Pons in a letter on November 20 "to do all in his power to put an end to the hindrances to international traffic and to re-establish freedom of circulation for persons and goods" in France.

A statement from the body said it had renewed its appeal to the minister on Monday, "requesting that assistance be provided to foreign lorry drivers, held hostage for more than a week without food or money."
The IRU said it had also written to European Union Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock on the issue, but gave no details.
